[ ALPIC BRAND GUIDE · V2 ]

Keep the mountain. Lead with the square.

Agents read a page in pieces. Squares gather into a mountain, a screen, or a word. Everything else supports that.

Six chapters for a presentation. The full draft still holds the audit and the open questions.

[ 01 — ORDER ]

One idea leads. The rest follows.

The elements already work. They compete because nothing says which one is in charge.

  1. HERO

    The square

    The one idea. One reveal per view.

  2. SUBJECT

    The mountain

    What the squares reveal most often.

  3. SUPPORT

    Tracks and type

    Diagonals, and three faces with one job each.

  4. ACCENT

    Berry, the arrow, one skier

    Small doses. One of each per view.

KEEP

  • The square mountain, with its trace, as the flagship.
  • Squares as data: traffic, tests, status.
  • The ↗ arrow and the bracket labels.

DROP

  • Ten hero treatments, and a second mountain in the same view.
  • Chairlifts, lodges, pines, blur, glitch and scanlines.
  • Greys and teals that are not in the palette.

[ 02 — MOUNTAIN ]

Four steps. Any peak.

The mountain is a recipe, not one fixed illustration.

Shade maps onto the midnight scale. Light maps onto the berry scale. Both scales are in the next chapter.

  • One mountain per view. The summit stays in the top third.
  • The base bleeds off the bottom, or off one side.
  • Text sits on the sky. If it must cross the mountain, use the trace.
  • One cell size. No blur, glitch, scanlines, or a sprite on the peak.

[ 04 — MARKS ]

Squares, tracks, one skier.

The square reveals. A track is the path an agent took. The skier is punctuation, and it always rides a track.

  • Squares never slide. They switch on the lattice, and a reveal ends on something real.
  • One cell size per piece. Trace nodes and track ends sit on that same lattice.
  • Three to five tracks. Irregular, one bend at most, square to square.
  • The skier stays off the hero, the nav and any data view. No groups, no chairlifts.

[ 05 — VOICE ]

Daylight for people. Night for builders.

A surface is one or the other. A long page may switch once. Type has three jobs, and berry is one phrase.

    [ THE SHIFT ]

  • One berry phrase per headline, at the end. Sentence case.
  • Labels sit in square brackets and stay under five words.
  • The ↗ is the only arrow. Corners stay square.
  • Status is a square: midnight passes, berry fails, border lime waits.

[ 06 — USE ]

Same moves, three places.

Homepage, docs, and a post. Then the calls that settle the rest.

[ TO MAKE SOMETHING LOOK LIKE ALPIC ]

Do these five things.

  1. Start with squares.

    One cell size, 4, 8 or 16 px. Everything sits on that lattice.

  2. Reveal one thing.

    A mountain first. Otherwise a screen, a word or a photo.

  3. Add a track.

    A few irregular diagonals, square to square, never level.

  4. Set the type.

    Mozilla Text, Inter, Roboto Mono. One berry phrase.

  5. Pick day or night.

    Buyers or builders. One arrow, one accent, one skier at most.

Cell sizes, the angle range and the motion timings are still proposals. The full list of open items is in the draft.
